clue.text: Stole from cupboard finally put on bishop in formal dress

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another follows it
the bishop's letter goes inside the word for formal dress

parts.note: a robe is a formal or ceremonial gown
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word cupboard

explanation.surface: A cleric in robes is caught pilfering from a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places D after ROBBE (B inside ROBE).
explanation.definitionFit: To rob someone is to steal from them, so the past tense is a direct synonym.

explanation.walkthrough: A rehoboam is a wine or champagne bottle holding six standard bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is an outsize wine bottle, so it holds a great quantity of drink.

clue.text: Bear being bowled? Disaster

a ruin is a disaster or downfall

clue.text: Say, good source of protein

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: A remark about something that is a good source of protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs are a classic protein-rich food, so one is a source of protein.

clue.text: Break up day with snarled-up traffic

explanation.definitionFit: To diffract light is to break it up into separate bands or a spectrum.

clue.text: Prisoner, maybe, one of an exclusive group

definitions.meaning: someone locked inside, as a prisoner is
a member of an inner circle

explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who is inside, such as a jailed convict; figuratively, a member of a privileged circle.

clue.text: Go faster, say, translating a trilogy

explanation.definitionFit: Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga collects three novels, making it a trilogy.

clue.text: One presenting an unwelcome task left incomplete by crew

explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman is the main presenter of a news broadcast.

clue.text: Swallowing 10cl, neat, may make one this?

definitions.text: Swallowing 10cl, neat, may make one this?

indicators.note: the word for neat swallows the measure, holding it inside

parts.note: tidy means neat
ten centilitres is a decilitre, abbreviated DL

explanation.surface: Downing a measure of spirit undiluted may leave you a little drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' works twice: as TIDY in the wordplay, and as undiluted drink in the whole reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, the likely effect of a neat measure of spirits.

clue.text: Screw top of jar I dropped into real mess

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, here of jar
the I is dropped into the middle of the other letters
making a mess of the word real jumbles its letters

explanation.surface: Someone unscrewing a jar lid drops it in a real mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' rearranges REAL to ALER, and I goes inside it to make AILER. Screw is British slang for a prison officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In prison slang a screw is a warder, the officer who locks up inmates.

clue.text: Refined rough girl, slim-waisted

clue.text: Sprinted, heading off being tracked down

parts.note: traced means tracked down

explanation.definitionFit: Raced and sprinted both mean ran at top speed.

clue.text: Store to have to keep one in always for Christmas, say

parts.note: to bank something is to store it

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the letter goes inside
in confirms the letter is placed inside

parts.note: to hold is to have
I is the Roman numeral one
ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Advice to keep stocks in all year round for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public holiday such as Christmas Day is called a bank holiday; AY is an old word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas Day is one example of a British public holiday, when banks close.

clue.text: A cat may be very nervous

definitions.meaning: a cat may literally give birth to kittens
a British idiom for being extremely anxious

explanation.surface: A cat might well be in a state of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally what a pregnant cat does; idiomatically, to get into a panic or tizzy.

clue.text: Two bits left smoother

parts.note: the two binary digits, 0 and 1, look like the letters O and I

explanation.surface: Two pieces remain from something smoother.
explanation.walkthrough: Binary bits are 0 and 1, which double as the letters O and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is a lubricant, something that makes motion or friction smoother.

clue.text: Being agitated may be a source of quarrels

explanation.surface: Being worked up might lead to arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrels' looks like arguments, but a quarrel is also an arrow-like crossbow bolt, kept in a quiver.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquiver means trembling with agitation or excitement.

clue.text: Sort of door sadly unproved to secure area

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so the anagram encloses the letter
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of unproved are disordered

explanation.surface: A door type that, regrettably, has not been shown to protect the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges UNPROVED, and 'to secure' wraps it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: An up-and-over door, common on garages, swings upwards and slides back over the opening.

clue.text: French city boundaries visited by ambassador

indicators.note: the boundaries are visited by the ambassador, who goes inside them

parts.note: rims are edges or boundaries
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.definitionFit: Rheims (Reims) is a cathedral city in Champagne, northeastern France.

clue.text: Assembly workers eating the last of their fried food

indicators.note: the last of picks the closing letter of their

explanation.surface: Factory workers on a break finishing their fried snacks.

clue.text: Hopeless sort of case one finally checks out?

clue.text: When one knocks out November, calendar gets less complicated

N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.walkthrough: One N of PLANNER is replaced by I.

clue.text: Airline no longer flying over a country

parts.note: Pan Am was a US airline that ceased operating in 1991

clue.text: Intensify struggle over stupid person abandoning pet

clue.text: Analysing joining the cast?

clue.text: A month's said to be stunning

parts.note: a May's: May is a month

clue.text: Doctor short Panorama feature

clue.text: Happens to be over ten? Apparently not

definitions.text: Happens to be over ten? Apparently not

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: is, as in it is so, means happens to be
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads 'IS over X', yet six is plainly not over ten, which the tail admits.
explanation.definitionFit: Six is less than ten, so the joking query and its denial both point to it.

clue.text: Axes regularly pronounced in surplus

explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of AXES, XS, and 'pronounced' says them aloud as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: An excess is an amount over what is needed, a surplus.
